### 3) Significant strengths and limitations by platform

**Microsoft Teams**
- **Strengths:** Deep Microsoft 365/LMS/SSO integration; strong admin/compliance/security controls; robust “hub” for class communication (chat/channels/files/meetings).
- **Limitations:** Can feel complex (navigation, notifications); best experience often depends on good tenant configuration and training.

**Google Meet**
- **Strengths:** Very low-friction web access; strong integration with Google Workspace (Calendar/Classroom where used); solid security posture and reliability.
- **Limitations:** Advanced teaching features (recording, attendance, controls) can be tier-dependent; generally less feature-dense than Teams for “all-in-one” collaboration.

**Zoom**
- **Strengths:** Excellent usability; strong synchronous teaching toolkit (breakouts, controls, classroom workflows) and broad device support.
- **Limitations:** Security/privacy is strong when configured well but historically scrutinized; some capabilities (webinars, expanded admin/reporting, storage) can increase cost.

**WhatsApp**
- **Strengths:** Extremely familiar and easy; fast, reliable small-group communication; end-to-end encryption for message content.
- **Limitations:** Not designed for formal instruction delivery (limited moderation, scheduling, recording, attendance, LMS integration); privacy/boundary concerns (phone numbers, metadata, informal channel).

**FaceTime**
- **Strengths:** High-quality calls; strong privacy model (end-to-end encryption); zero additional licensing cost for Apple users.
- **Limitations:** Severe ecosystem constraints for a university (Apple-centric participation); minimal classroom management features and limited enterprise admin/integration.

**Skype**
- **Strengths:** Low cost and basic calling/chat works across platforms.
- **Limitations:** Weaker modern LMS/enterprise integration and classroom features; declining relevance in many institutions in favor of Teams; less robust support/training pathways for campus-scale deployment.
